CIV.note: No rule or authority on AI harms is stated.
The AI forecasting is inside the health supply chain, a sector system, not general administration.

facts.fact: The DHIS2 conference abstract says the Ministry of Health selected 52 health facilities to receive monthly AI-driven forecasts for 11 family planning commodities, delivered by Pendulum through mSupply Mobile, with delivery to about 1,000 facilities planned for 2024.
facts.system: Pendulum AI forecasting via mSupply Mobile

facts.fact: The abstract's authors report that Pendulum's family planning model, built on data from 2,500+ facilities, gave forecasts 38% more accurate than traditional methods, and that a 2023 national malaria programme proof of concept on 36 commodities cut forecasting error by an average of 37%.
facts.system: Pendulum AI forecasting via mSupply Mobile

CIV.note: No AI strategy or policy is mentioned.
The model is built by an outside company, Pendulum; no local development or AI computing in the country is stated.
Names DHIS2, eSIGL and mSupply (a logistics LMIS) as data sources, but states nothing on HMIS or EMR coverage, tiers or clinics.
DHIS2 is named as a data source only; the abstract does not say that a national system is in service or what facilities report through it.
